To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a 64-bpt AT-rich region of the upstream apo(a) promoter contains multiple liver-specific binding sites for transcriptional activators, and that the 64-bp cis-element contains three dyad symmetry sequences (DSEs).
we have identified a 5' upstream 64-bp region in the apo(a) gene that contains multiple binding sites for liver-specific factors that activate apo(a) transcription in vitro and in vivo.
the apo(a) gene contains a 64-bps cis-element, that is essential for its transcriptional activation, and that this element binds to multiple liver specific factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the mechanism of liver-specific transcriptional control of the apo(a) gene.
the identification of the liver-specific factors that bind to the 64-bp upstream element and activate the apo(a) gene in liver cells.
the molecular mechanisms of the liver-specific transcription of apo(a) gene and the identification of liver-specific transcription factors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 64-bp cis-element of apo(a) gene contains DSEs that bind to multiple liver-specific transcription factors.
the apo(a) gene contains both positive and negative regulatory elements, and that the 64 bp region is crucial for the expression of the gene in liver cells.
the apo(a) promoter is a composite promoter with both positive and negative regulatory domains, which is responsible for liver-specific expression of the apo(a) gene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the apo(a) gene contains a liver-specific promoter and a negative regulatory region that are regulated by multiple transcription factors and transcriptional repressors.
the apo(a) gene contains multiple cis-elements that are crucial for its transcription in liver.
the 64-bp cis-element is the major regulatory region for apo(a) gene expression in liver.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the apo(a) gene expression is regulated by multiple liver-specific factors, which may be involved in the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis.
the liver-specific factors bind cooperatively to multiple sites in the apo(a) gene promoter and that the 64-bp DSEs are crucial for the binding.

the 64 bp cis-acting element of the apo(a) gene contains three DSEs and that both DSEs are required for the binding of multiple liver-specific factors to the 64 bp element, for synergistic binding and for the activation of the apo(a).
